title: I made Veinward, a cozy first-person mining incremental game
author: ViolinistTemporary
selftext:
Veinward is a first-person incremental game inspired by Minecraft Prison servers. You dig down through a deep, cel-shaded mine and get stronger with every trip. A block that takes ten swings at the start breaks in one hit later on, and after that, whole walls go with a single blast. You start out selling ore for a handful of credits, then it's hundreds, thousands, millions, and eventually billions. The caves that gave you trouble early on take seconds to clear.

Above the mine, there's a cozy little town, full of bright colors. You sell your ore there, forge better pickaxes, and build your own house piece by piece. In the saloon, you can grab a drink for a boost before your next trip or sit down at the blackjack and roulette tables. There's also a cat you can pet.

There are a lot of skills, and they change how you play. You can fire a grapple hook and get pulled across a cavern, strap on a jetpack to rise out of the mine, throw your pickaxe and watch it ricochet through the rock, or turn on Blast Strike so every swing leaves a crater.

You also set up auto miners that keep digging while you do something else, and you smelt ore into ingots and turn them into runes for different pickaxe builds. Hidden collectibles that give permanent boosts are scattered around the map for you to find. When progress slows down, you rebirth, come back much stronger, and try a different build.

The demo is free and about 2-3 hours, and there's a lot more on the way, expect major content updates before the full release.
